scope: Shared bounded settings receipt validation and independent complete-pair restoration
findings: AIProfileYield validated data but direct player/specialist/stop cleanup bypassed that validation.
AIRestoreProfile could consume original baselines without matching applied values, losing future restoration information.
Fractional negative aim values between -1 and0 passed the old absent-sentinel validation.
A precision-excluded first profile captured an aim baseline despite never acquiring its coefficient.
implementation: Read-only AIProfileReceipt returns detached supported9-key finite0..1 maps, strict -1-or-nonnegative finite aim values, independent ready/pending flags and application readiness.
Actual-owner atomic restoration reads the same shared contract; invalid metadata does not authorise writes or deletion.
Only complete skill or aim pairs may be restored/retired. The other pending pair and variance remain; changed native values are preserved.
Application refuses orphan applied data rather than recapturing it as original.
Fresh precision-excluded profiles acquire no aim baseline. An existing coefficient pair retires only after observed native restoration; no-applied state is not repeatedly published as nil.
No new worker, world scan, movement/target command, timeout or mission-owner reset.
source_intent: Continue the existing exact baseline/applied ownership design and source-review preference for finite holds with real release. No additional Workshop method is claimed as ported by this validation change.
limits: Separate object variables still do not prove ordered delivery or distinguish a never-profiled unit from missing initial replication.
Pending baseline data may remain indefinitely without a later safe caller; no eventual-restoration or provider-handback completion is claimed.
Same-value edits cannot establish writer identity. Physical stop/exclusion/partial delivery and owner migration remain unverified.
Bounded map validation/copy cost and runtime overhead are unmeasured; accepted performance budgets remain outstanding.
progress: Existing build-out scores unchanged; current dependencies reassessed.
